csat-01.title: Number System: Unit Digit Cyclicity & Exponent Powers
csat-01.mental_model: Ferris Wheel Loop: Divide the power by 4. The remainder gives the step on the 4-spoke wheel. Digits 0, 1, 5, 6 never change.

questions.topic: Number System: Unit Digit Cyclicity & Exponent Powers
questions.q: In an administrative data encryption system, a security key is generated using the expression (202)^50. What is the units digit of this resulting key value?
questions.child_logic: Ferris Wheel Loop: The base ends in 2, which has a 4-step cyclicity. Divide the power 50 by 4: remainder is 2. 2^2 ends in 4!
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Focus only on the unit digit of the base, which is 2.
Step 2: Cyclicity of 2 is 4. Divide power 50 by 4: 50 = 4 * 12 + 2.
Step 3: Effective power is 2. 2^2 = 4, whose unit digit is 4.
Step 4: Hence, the unit digit is 4.

csat-02.title: Number System: Remainder Theorem & Successive Division
csat-02.mental_model: Elevator Floors: Work backwards from quotient to reconstruct N. Use binomial expansion shortcuts for large powers.

questions.topic: Number System: Remainder Theorem & Successive Division
questions.q: A government food grain consignment containing (8)^47 metric tons of wheat is to be distributed equally among 7 state relief warehouses. What will be the leftover undistributed balance in metric tons?
questions.child_logic: Binomial Balance: Notice that 8 is close to 7 (8 = 7 + 1). The remainder is simply (+1)^47 mod 7 = 1!
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Express base relative to divisor: 8 = 7 * 1 + 1.
Step 2: By Binomial theorem, (8)^47 mod 7 = (+1)^47 mod 7.
Step 3: (+1)^47 evaluates to 1.
Step 4: Leftover balance is 1 metric tons.

questions.child_logic: Binomial Balance: Notice that 18 is close to 19 (18 = 19 - 1). The remainder is simply (-1)^166 mod 19 = 1!
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Express base relative to divisor: 18 = 19 * 1 - 1.
Step 2: By Binomial theorem, (18)^166 mod 19 = (-1)^166 mod 19.
Step 3: (-1)^166 evaluates to 1.
Step 4: Leftover balance is 1 metric tons.

csat-03.title: Number System: Divisibility Rules (3, 7, 9, 11, 13, 72, 88, 99)
csat-03.mental_model: Digit Hopscotch: Alternating digit difference for 11. Sum of digits for 3 and 9. Last 3 digits for 8.

questions.topic: Number System: Divisibility Rules (3, 7, 9, 11, 13, 72, 88, 99)
questions.q: A district administration assigns a 6-digit identification code 45x78y to rural development projects. If this code is known to be completely divisible by 72, what is the value of (2x + y)?
questions.child_logic: Two Guards: 72 = 8 x 9. Guard 8 inspects the last 3 digits (78y): 784 is divisible by 8, so y = 4. Guard 9 checks sum of digits: 28 + x must be divisible by 9, so x = 8. 2(8) + 4 = 20!
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Divisibility by 8 requires last 3 digits 78y to be divisible by 8. 784 / 8 = 98, so y = 4.
Step 2: Divisibility by 9 requires sum of digits (4+5+x+7+8+4 = 28+x) to be a multiple of 9. Nearest multiple is 36, giving x = 8.
Step 3: Compute 2x + y = 2(8) + 4 = 16 + 4 = 20.

questions.topic: Number System: Divisibility Rules (3, 7, 9, 11, 13, 72, 88, 99)
questions.q: An auditor discovers a 7-digit file identifier 738a6b2 is strictly divisible by 88. What is the value of (a + b)?
questions.child_logic: Teamwork Check: 88 = 8 x 11. Check last 3 digits 6b2 for 8 (b=3), then balance odd and even position digit sums for 11 to get a=6. a + b = 9!
questions.explanation:
Step 1: 6b2 must be divisible by 8. 632 / 8 = 79, so b = 3.
Step 2: Alternating sum test for 11: (2 + 6 + 8 + 7) - (3 + a + 3) = 23 - (6 + a) = 17 - a. For divisibility by 11, 17 - a = 11 -> a = 6.
Step 3: a + b = 6 + 3 = 9.

csat-04.mental_model: Spice Jars: If N = p^a * q^b, total factors = (a+1)(b+1). Product of factors = N^(Total/2).

questions.topic: Number System: Factors, Multiples & Prime Factorization
questions.q: A municipal corporation plans to demarcate a civic park of area 360 square meters into identical rectangular sub-plots of integer dimensions. In how many distinct ways can the dimensions (length and width) be chosen?
questions.child_logic: Spice Jar Pairs: Find total factors of 360 = 24. Every factor pair (L x W) forms one rectangular dimension. Number of ways = 12!
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Prime factorize 360: {2: 3, 3: 2, 5: 1}.
Step 2: Total factors = 24.
Step 3: Distinct dimension pairs = ceil(24 / 2) = 12.

csat-05.title: Number System: Trailing Zeroes in Factorials & Products
csat-05.mental_model: Shoe Pair Machine: Zeroes come from 2 x 5 pairs. Count the scarce 5s: [N/5] + [N/25] + [N/125].

questions.topic: Number System: Trailing Zeroes in Factorials & Products
questions.q: A digital census calculation requires multiplying all integers from 1 up to 60. How many consecutive zeroes will appear at the end of the calculated product?
questions.child_logic: Shoe Pair Factory: Zeroes are created by 2 x 5 pairs. Count the scarce 5s: [60/5] + [60/25] = 14 pairs!
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Trailing zeroes equal the highest power of 5 in 60!.
Step 2: Apply Legendre's formula: sum of floor(60 / 5^k).
Step 3: Total zeroes = 14.

questions.q: A digital census calculation requires multiplying all integers from 1 up to 300. How many consecutive zeroes will appear at the end of the calculated product?
questions.child_logic: Shoe Pair Factory: Zeroes are created by 2 x 5 pairs. Count the scarce 5s: [300/5] + [300/25] = 74 pairs!
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Trailing zeroes equal the highest power of 5 in 300!.
Step 2: Apply Legendre's formula: sum of floor(300 / 5^k).
Step 3: Total zeroes = 74.

csat-06.title: Percentages: The ₹100 Bill Method & Fraction-Percentage Ladder
csat-06.mental_model: ₹100 Bill Anchor: Anchor unknown base to 100. 1/6 = 16.67%, 1/7 = 14.28%, 1/8 = 12.5%.

questions.topic: Percentages: The ₹100 Bill Method & Fraction-Percentage Ladder
questions.q: Due to supply disruption, the retail price of edible oil rises by 15%. By what percentage must an urban household curb its consumption so that its monthly budget remains completely unchanged?
questions.child_logic: The ₹100 Bill Anchor: If initial price was ₹100 for 100 units, new price is ₹115. To spend only ₹100, reduction = [15 / 115] x 100 = 13.0%!
questions.explanation:
Formula: Consumption reduction % = [r / (100 + r)] * 100.
Substitute r = 15%: [15 / 115] * 100 = 13.0%.

csat-07.mental_model: Net Effect Formula: Net % = a + b + (ab/100). Equal rise then fall always produces a net loss.

questions.topic: Percentages: Successive Changes, Population & Compounding
questions.q: The population of a smart city district grew by 12% in the first year and by 18% in the second year. What was the net compound percentage growth over the two-year period?
questions.child_logic: Interest on Interest: Net % = a + b + (ab/100) = 12 + 18 + (12*18/100) = 32.2%!
questions.explanation:
Successive formula: Net % = a + b + (a*b)/100.
Substitute a = 12, b = 18: 12 + 18 + (216/100) = 32.2%.

questions.topic: Profit and Loss: Markup, Discounts & Faulty Balances

csat-09.title: Averages: The Playground Seesaw Balancing Scale & Cricket Innings
csat-09.mental_model: Seesaw Balancing: Sum of positive deviations = Sum of negative deviations from average.

questions.topic: Averages: The Playground Seesaw Balancing Scale & Cricket Innings
questions.q: The average marks of 21 candidates in a civil services test series was computed as 46. Subsequently, an error was detected where an original score of 36 was erroneously recorded as 76. What is the correct rectified average?
questions.child_logic: Seesaw Deficit: The recorded score was 40 marks too high! Deduct 40 marks distributed equally across all 21 candidates: drop = 40/21.
questions.explanation:
Net change in total = 36 - 76 = -40 marks.
Change in average = -40 / 21 = -1.9.
Rectified average = 46 + (-1.9) = 44.1.

questions.child_logic: Alligation Cross: Diagonal differences give the mixing ratio! (52 - 33) : (33 - 21) = 19 : 12 = 19 : 12!
questions.explanation:
By Rule of Alligation:
Cheaper Qty / Dearer Qty = (Dearer Price - Mean Price) / (Mean Price - Cheaper Price)
= (52 - 33) / (33 - 21) = 19 / 12 = 19/12.

csat-11.title: Time and Work: The LCM Brick Wall & Alternate Days
csat-11.mental_model: Brick Wall: Total work = LCM of days. Daily output = Work / Days. Alternate days = 2-day cycle.

questions.topic: Time and Work: The LCM Brick Wall & Alternate Days
questions.q: Officer P can audit a district revenue portfolio in 11 days working alone. Officer Q can complete the identical audit in 16 days. If both officers collaborate simultaneously, in how many days will the audit be finalized?
questions.child_logic: LCM Brick Wall: Total work = LCM(11, 16) = 176 audit files. P audits 16 files/day, Q audits 11 files/day. Together = 27 files/day. Days = 176 / 27 = 6.5 days!

csat-12.title: Pipes and Cisterns: Inlets vs Outlets & Leaks
csat-12.mental_model: Bathtub Inflow-Outflow: Inlets add positive units, leaks subtract negative units.

questions.topic: Pipes and Cisterns: Inlets vs Outlets & Leaks
questions.q: An inlet canal pipe can fill a municipal drinking water reservoir in 7 hours. However, an undetected subterranean seepage empties the full reservoir in 13 hours. If the inlet is left running continuously, how many hours will it take to fill the reservoir completely?
questions.child_logic: Inflow minus Outflow: Capacity = LCM(7, 13) = 91 units. Inflow = +13/hr, Leak = -7/hr. Net inflow = +6 units/hr. Total time = 91/6 = 15.2 hours!
questions.explanation:
Net filling rate per hour = 1/7 - 1/13 = (6)/(91).
Time = (91) / (6) = 15.2 hours.

csat-13.title: Time, Speed & Distance: 5/18 Converter & Harmonic Average Speed
csat-13.mental_model: Equal Distance Trap: If distance is same, average speed = 2xy/(x+y). Convert km/h to m/s via 5/18.

questions.topic: Time, Speed & Distance: 5/18 Converter & Harmonic Average Speed
questions.q: A relief convoy travels from District Headquarters to a flood-affected subdivision at an average speed of 35 km/h and returns to Headquarters along the identical route at 56 km/h. What is the average speed of the convoy for the complete round trip?
questions.child_logic: Equal Distance Trap: Because the distance is identical in both directions, average speed is the Harmonic Mean: 2*x*y / (x+y) = 2*35*56 / (91) = 43.1 km/h! Never take arithmetic average.
questions.explanation: Average speed = Total Distance / Total Time = 2D / (D/35 + D/56) = 2*s1*s2 / (s1 + s2) = 2*35*56 / (91) = 43.1 km/h.

questions.child_logic: Equal Distance Trap: Because the distance is identical in both directions, average speed is the Harmonic Mean: 2*x*y / (x+y) = 2*65*92 / (157) = 76.2 km/h! Never take arithmetic average.
questions.explanation: Average speed = Total Distance / Total Time = 2D / (D/65 + D/92) = 2*s1*s2 / (s1 + s2) = 2*65*92 / (157) = 76.2 km/h.

csat-14.title: Trains: Crossing Poles vs Platforms & Relative Speeds
csat-14.mental_model: Moving Bridge: Crossing a pole takes distance L. Crossing a platform takes distance (L + P).

questions.topic: Trains: Crossing Poles vs Platforms & Relative Speeds
questions.q: A special civil services inspection train of length 175 meters is traveling at a uniform speed of 63 km/h. How many seconds will it take to completely pass over a railway station platform of length 230 meters?
questions.child_logic: Moving Bridge: To clear the platform, the train must cover its OWN length PLUS the platform length: 175 + 230 = 405 m. Speed = 63 x 5/18 = 17.5 m/s. Time = 405 / 17.5 = 23.1 s!
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Convert speed to m/s: 63 * (5/18) = 17.5 m/s.
Step 2: Total distance = Train Length + Platform Length = 175 + 230 = 405 m.
Step 3: Time = Distance / Speed = 405 / 17.5 = 23.1 seconds.

csat-16.title: Permutations & Combinations: Handshake Theorem, Tie Method & Gap Method
csat-16.mental_model: Party Handshakes: n people shaking hands = n(n-1)/2. To keep items together, tie them into one super-item.

questions.topic: Permutations & Combinations: Handshake Theorem, Tie Method & Gap Method
questions.q: At an international inter-governmental conference, 11 delegates assemble in a plenary chamber. If every delegate exchanges exactly one formal handshake with every other delegate present, what is the total number of handshakes exchanged?
questions.child_logic: Party Handshake Rule: n people shake hands = n(n-1)/2. Each handshake takes 2 people: 11 x 10 / 2 = 55 handshakes!
questions.explanation: Total combinations of selecting 2 delegates from 11 = C(11, 2) = (11 * (11 - 1)) / 2 = 55.

csat-17.title: Probability: Complementary Odds, Dice, Bags & Coins
csat-17.mental_model: Complementary Shortcut: Probability of 'at least one' = 1 - Probability of 'none'.

questions.topic: Probability: Complementary Odds, Dice, Bags & Coins
questions.q: In a cryptographic audit protocol, a fair verification coin is tossed independently 4 consecutive times. What is the probability of securing at least one 'Heads' outcome across the series?
questions.child_logic: Complementary Trick: Probability of 'at least one' = 1 - P(none)! Total outcomes = 2^4 = 16. The only failure is ALL tails (1 outcome). Favorable = 16 - 1 = 15!
questions.explanation: P(at least one Head) = 1 - P(no Heads) = 1 - (1/2)^4 = 1 - 1/16 = 15/16.

csat-19.mental_model: 7-Day Wheel: Ordinary year = 1 odd day; Leap year = 2 odd days. 100 years = 5 odd days, 400 years = 0.

questions.topic: Calendar: The 7-Day Cycle, Odd Days & Century Repeats
questions.q: If the Republic Day (26th January) of a given non-leap year falls on a Monday, what day of the week will Republic Day fall on exactly 5 years later (assuming 1 leap year(s) intervene)?
questions.child_logic: 7-Day Wheel: Each ordinary year advances by 1 odd day; each leap year advances by 2 odd days. Net odd days = 5 + 1 = 6. 6 mod 7 = 6 steps from Monday -> Sunday!
questions.explanation:
Odd days = (Ordinary years * 1) + (Leap years * 2) = (4 * 1) + (1 * 2) = 6.
6 mod 7 = 6 days.
Advancing 6 days from Monday yields Sunday.

csat-20.title: Cubes and Dice: Opposite Faces & Cut Painted Cubes
csat-20.mental_model: Rubik's Layers: In n x n x n cube: 3-face = 8, 2-face = 12(n-2), 1-face = 6(n-2)^2, 0-face = (n-2)^3.

questions.topic: Cubes and Dice: Opposite Faces & Cut Painted Cubes
questions.q: A solid wooden cube of side 4 cm is painted blue on all outer faces and subsequently cut into unit cubes of side 1 cm. How many smaller cubes have exactly two painted faces?
questions.child_logic: Rubik's Edge Strips: 2-painted faces reside along the edges (excluding the corners). In an 4x4 cube with 12 edges: Count = 12 x (n - 2) = 12 x (4 - 2) = 24 cubes!
questions.explanation:
In an n x n x n painted cube:
- 3-face painted (corners) = 8
- 2-face painted (edges) = 12(n - 2) = 12(4 - 2) = 24
- 1-face painted (centers) = 6(n - 2)^2 = 24
- 0-face painted (core) = (n - 2)^3 = 8.

questions.child_logic: Rubik's Edge Strips: 2-painted faces reside along the edges (excluding the corners). In an 3x3 cube with 12 edges: Count = 12 x (n - 2) = 12 x (3 - 2) = 12 cubes!
questions.explanation:
In an n x n x n painted cube:
- 3-face painted (corners) = 8
- 2-face painted (edges) = 12(n - 2) = 12(3 - 2) = 12
- 1-face painted (centers) = 6(n - 2)^2 = 6
- 0-face painted (core) = (n - 2)^3 = 1.

csat-21.title: Blood Relations: Generation Family Tree Mapping & Coded Relations
csat-21.mental_model: Generation Ladder: Draw vertical lines for generation changes (+1 parent, -1 child), horizontal for siblings.

questions.topic: Blood Relations: Generation Family Tree Mapping & Coded Relations
questions.q: Examining a family genealogical chart, an officer observes: 'A is the brother of B. C is the father of A. D is the sister of E. E is the daughter of B.' How is D related to A?
questions.child_logic: Generation Ladder: E is daughter of B, and D is sister of E -> D is also child of B. Since A is brother of B, B's daughter D is the niece of A!
questions.explanation:
Step 1: B is parent of E. D and E are sisters, so B is parent of D.
Step 2: A is brother of B.
Step 3: Brother of parent is uncle. Therefore, D is the niece of A.

questions.child_logic: Generation Ladder: E is daughter of B, and D is sister of E -> D is also child of B. Since A is brother of B, B's daughter D is the niece of A!
questions.explanation:
Step 1: B is parent of E. D and E are sisters, so B is parent of D.
Step 2: A is brother of B.
Step 3: Brother of parent is uncle. Therefore, D is the niece of A.

csat-22.title: Direction Sense: 8-Point Compass & Pythagoras Trajectory
csat-22.mental_model: Right Triangle: Net displacement = sqrt(East-West^2 + North-South^2). Shadow at sunset is towards East.

questions.topic: Direction Sense: 8-Point Compass & Pythagoras Trajectory
questions.q: A forest ranger patrols 13 km directly North from the base camp, then executes a 90° clockwise turn and rides 6 km directly East. What is the shortest straight-line Euclidean distance back to the base camp?
questions.child_logic: Pythagoras Trajectory: Forms a right-angled triangle with legs 13 km and 6 km. Shortest distance = sqrt(13^2 + 6^2) = 14 km!
questions.explanation: Net displacement = sqrt(North^2 + East^2) = sqrt(13^2 + 6^2) = sqrt(205) = 14 km.

csat-23.title: Syllogisms: Mom & Baby Venn Circles & Either-Or Rules
csat-23.mental_model: Mom and Baby Kangaroo: 'All A are B' places circle A inside pouch B. Either-or pair requires complementary pair.

questions.topic: Syllogisms: Mom & Baby Venn Circles & Either-Or Rules
questions.q:
Consider the following statements and conclusions:
Statements:
1. All IAS officers are public servants.
2. No public servant accepts unauthorized gratuities.
3. Some economists are IAS officers.

Conclusions:
I. No IAS officer accepts unauthorized gratuities.
II. Some economists are public servants.

Which of the conclusions logically follow?
questions.child_logic: Mom & Baby Kangaroo Venn: IAS is inside Public Servants pouch. Gratuities is completely outside. So no IAS touches Gratuities (I holds). Economists overlap IAS, which is inside Public Servants (II holds)!
questions.explanation:
Conclusion I: IAS is subset of Public Servants; Public Servants is disjoint from Gratuities -> IAS is disjoint from Gratuities (Valid).
Conclusion II: Economists overlap IAS, and IAS is subset of Public Servants -> Economists overlap Public Servants (Valid).
Both I and II follow.

csat-24.title: Seating Arrangements & Complex Puzzles (Linear & Circular)
csat-24.mental_model: Definite Anchor First: Place the person with fixed position first. Note facing center vs facing outside.

questions.topic: Seating Arrangements & Complex Puzzles (Linear & Circular)
questions.q: Six diplomats (U, V, W, X, Y, Z) sit around a circular conference table facing the center. U sits directly between V and W. X sits second to the right of W. Y sits adjacent to V. Who sits diametrically opposite to U?
questions.child_logic: Circle Anchor: Place U at bottom. V is left, W is right. X is 2nd right of W -> X lands directly opposite U on the 6-seat circle!
questions.explanation: Fix positions: 1: U. 2: V (left). 6: W (right). 2nd right from 6 (moving counter-clockwise: 1, then 2, wait: if facing center, right of 6 is 5 then 4). Position 4 is opposite Position 1 (U). X sits at 4. Hence X is directly opposite U.

questions.child_logic: Circle Anchor: Place U at bottom. V is left, W is right. X is 2nd right of W -> X lands directly opposite U on the 6-seat circle!
questions.explanation: Fix positions: 1: U. 2: V (left). 6: W (right). 2nd right from 6 (moving counter-clockwise: 1, then 2, wait: if facing center, right of 6 is 5 then 4). Position 4 is opposite Position 1 (U). X sits at 4. Hence X is directly opposite U.

csat-25.title: Reading Comprehension: The 4-Step 'Sherlocking' Method (Crux, Corollaries & Assumptions)
csat-25.mental_model: Sherlock Rule: Reject external assumptions. Extreme words ('only', 'never', 'all') are almost always traps.

questions.topic: Reading Comprehension: The 4-Step 'Sherlocking' Method (Crux, Corollaries & Assumptions)
questions.q:
Read the following excerpt with analytical care:

"The governance of public digital infrastructure cannot be left solely to market forces. When essential civic services—from subsidy disbursement to digital health registries—depend on proprietary platforms, democratic accountability is compromised by black-box algorithms and vendor lock-in."

Which one of the following best reflects the most logical and critical inference from the passage?
options: (a) Digital technology should be prohibited in core government welfare programs.
(b) Public digital architecture demands sovereign open standards and democratic oversight.
(c) Private software vendors are incapable of delivering technical efficiency.
(d) Citizens should revert to paper-based administrative documentation.
questions.child_logic: Sherlock Rule: Identify the author's primary conflict: private proprietary lock-in vs democratic accountability. The solution is sovereign open public infrastructure.
questions.explanation: The author critiques proprietary dependency in civic services. Option (b) directly captures the logical necessity of sovereign public governance. Options (a) and (d) are extreme reactionary distractors; (c) makes an unsupported blanket assertion.

questions.topic: Reading Comprehension: The 4-Step 'Sherlocking' Method (Crux, Corollaries & Assumptions)
questions.q:
Read the following excerpt with analytical care:

"Fiscal decentralization without commensurate administrative capacity at local government levels leads to resource misallocation rather than empowerment. Devolving funds to panchayats without accounting expertise or auditing personnel merely transfers bureaucratic bottlenecks downwards."

Which one of the following is the most crucial assumption implied in the passage?
options: (a) Local governments are inherently more prone to fiscal irregularities than central authorities.
(b) Effective utilization of devolved public funds requires trained administrative and auditing manpower.
(c) Financial allocations to rural local bodies should be halted until digital systems are fully deployed.
(d) Centralized administration always produces superior governance outcomes.
questions.child_logic: Assumption Hunt: Why does fiscal devolution without capacity cause misallocation? Because fund utilization assumes skilled manpower! That is the unstated logical bridge.
questions.explanation: The argument asserts that devolution fails when technical capacity is missing. The unstated premise is that administrative expertise is a necessary condition for fiscal efficiency (Option b). Other options are extreme or unjustified.

questions.topic: Reading Comprehension: The 4-Step 'Sherlocking' Method (Crux, Corollaries & Assumptions)
questions.q:
Read the following excerpt with analytical care:

"Soil degradation is rarely an instantaneous ecological collapse; it is an incremental attrition caused by uncalibrated nitrogenous subsidies, monoculture crop rotations, and depleted organic carbon. Because its economic costs remain deferred across generations, market price signals fail to trigger timely corrective conservation."

Which one of the following is the most valid logical corollary from the passage?
options: (a) Agricultural markets and subsidy regimes must internalize long-term ecological soil health costs.
(b) Chemical fertilizer application should be criminalized with immediate effect.
(c) Private farming is fundamentally incompatible with ecological sustainability.
(d) Food grain production must be decreased to arrest soil erosion.
questions.child_logic: Sherlock Rule: Market price signals fail because costs are deferred across generations. The logical corollary is that pricing and subsidies must account for ecological costs.
questions.explanation: The passage diagnoses market failure due to deferred environmental costs. Option (a) directly remedies this failure. Options (b), (c), and (d) are extreme and illogical.
